Package hadur117.micro.core

Class Targeting

java.lang.Object
hadur117.micro.core.Targeting
public final class Targeting extends Object
The gun: a per-opponent Markov chain over the target's movement state (Figment), played forward by Monte-Carlo to bullet arrival and voted into angle bins. One change of substance: a state whose row holds fewer than WARM samples is not sampled but held, so the playout continues at the scan's speed and turn rate, which is circular projection (SAOR-6); once a row holds WARM or more, successors are drawn from it (SAOR-7).

A state packs acceleration sign (3 values), integer speed (17) and turn in half steps of the engine's largest turn at the last speed (5) into one int below STATES. A row is a char[] of ROW + 1: successors in the first ROW slots, the count of transitions seen in the last. Chars rather than Figment's ints keep 512 opponents' tables at Figment's 75 MB for 256.

    • record

      public static void record(char[] row, int state)
      Records that state followed the row's state. Figment's idiom, quirk included: no bounds check, so the sample after the ROWth lands on the count slot and the count becomes that state's value. A count past the row then makes the store throw, the adapter's catch absorbs it and the count runs on; a count below it resumes writing over old samples. Reads take the count modulo ROW.
      Parameters:
      row - the row of the state the target was in at its scan before
      state - the state it is in now
